Final for Publication

File No. 23029T1

17-13-0303-C(1) Substitute Type 1 Narrative & Plans — 526 North Western Avenue. Chicago,
IL

Proposed Zoning: C1-3 Neighborhood Commercial District
Lot Area: 8,220 sq. ft.

Proposed Land Use: The Applicant is proposing to redevelop the subject property with a new
five-story mixed-use building containing 1,830 sq. ft. of commercial/retail
space and an off-street parking garage on the first floor and nine (9)
residential dwelling units above. The proposed building will measure
approximately 58 ft.-9 in. in height. The subject property is a Transit Served
Location and will be supported by nine (9) off-street garage parking spaces.
Pursuant to Sec. 17-13-0303-D optional Administrative Adjustment and
Variation and pursuant to Secs. 17-13-1003-EE and 17-13-1101-B of the
Chicago Zoning Ordinance, the Applicant is seeking to increase the
residential off-street parking ratio from 55.5% (5 parking spaces) to 100%
(9 parking spaces), reduce the rear setback for floors containing residential
units from 30 feet to 5 ft., and is seeking all relief necessary, as allowed by
the Chicago Zoning Code, for the attached plans.

(A) _ The Project’s Floor Area Ratio: 23,467 square feet (2.85 FAR)

(B) The Project’s Density (Minimum Lot Area Per D.U.): 913.33 square feet per D.U.
(9 residential units)

© The amount of off-street parking: 9 parking spaces total

*The subject property is a designated Transit Served Location based on its
proximity to Western CTA Bus Route. Pursuant to Sec. 17-13-1003-EE, the
Applicant is seeking to increase the off-street parking ratio from 55.5% (5 parking
spaces) to 100% (9 parking spaces).

(D) Setbacks:
a. Front Setback: 12 inches
b. Side Setbacks:
North Side: 2 feet
South Side: 12 inches
c Rear Setback: 5 feet

*Pursuant to Sec. 17-13-1101-B, the Applicant is seeking to reduce the rear setback
for floors containing residential units from 30 feet to 5 feet.

(E) Building Height: 58 feet-9 inches

Final for Publication

Sec. 17-3-0308 Criteria for Transit-Served Locations — Supplemental Narrative Zoning Analysis

1. The subject property is a designated Transit Served Location per Sec. 17-10-0102-B
because it is located within approximately 344 linear feet of the Western CTA Bus Route
(Route 49). The proposed mixed-use building containing one (1) commercial space anda
parking garage on the first floor and nine (9) residential units above will be supported by
nine (9) off-street parking spaces. Pursuant to Section 17-13-1003-EE, the Applicant is
seeking to permit an increase in the residential off-street parking ratio from 55.5% (5

parking spaces) to 100% (9 parking spaces).

2. The proposed building complies with the main building door and entryway design
standards provided by Sec. 17-4-0504. The proposed building will have a front setback of
12 inches from the subject lot’s front property line along North Western Avenue to align
with the footprints of the neighboring buildings on the block, The building’s first floor was
designed with widows facing the sidewalk located along North Western Avenue.

3. The Transit Friendly Development Guide defines “transit friendly development’ as
development which is oriented towards and integrated with adjacent transit. The proposed
mixed-use building incorporates accessibility and connectivity to mass transit based on its
location near the Western CTA Bus Route. The Applicant believes the redevelopment of
an underutilized lot will improve the subject area for residents and other commuters

traveling in the subject area.

4. The proposed mixed-use building will contain approximately 1,830 sq. ft. of commercial
space on the first floor and nine (9) residential units above. The proposed building will be
supported by nine (9) off-street parking spaces. The Applicant is seeking administrative
approval to permit the off-street parking increase for the residential units pursuant to the

TOD Ordinance.

5. The Applicant believes the proposed mixed-use building will provide appropriate density
in the subject neighborhood. More specifically, the project will replace a commercial
building with a new mixed-use building, which will provide additional residential housing
thereby meeting market demand. Based on the subject property’s proximity to a designated
CTA Bus Route (Western — Route 49), the Applicant believes the project provides transit
options and otherwise complies with the Travel Demand Study and Management Plan rules
promulgated by the Department of Transportation by serving an area in need.
